title: Spike Telescope: latency vs cost annotated notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, exploratory benchmark run that we called the 'Spike Telescope' sweep: a set of small targeted microburst experiments designed to show how per-token cost and latency percentiles evolve as we zoom from sustained QPS down to sub-second burst events. The goal is a concise, shareable one-pager that product and SRE can use to reason about fast-fallback policies and admission thresholds.

Key takeaway (short):
- Small microbursts (<300ms, 5–40 concurrent short sessions) cause disproportionate p99 amplification vs cost.
- Two low-effort mitigations (tight slotization + opportunistic prefetch) gave most of the p99 benefit with <7% unit-cost increase in our run.

Methodology (brief):
- Workloads: three synthetic profiles approximating real traffic slices:
  1) chat-quick: requests with 8–32 tokens output, 120–180ms model compute mean.
  2) assistant: 40–200 tokens output, mixed compute (median 300ms).
  3) multimodal-probe: 60–400 tokens, heavier compute, used sparingly.
- Injection: we ran bursts by injecting groups of sessions at arrival spikes of 50, 100, 250 qps sustained for 200ms–3s to simulate microbursts.
- Configs tested (representative labels):
  A. baseline-multiplex (default multiplex scheduler, 64ms slot granularity)
  B. slot-tight (32ms slots, earlier preemption)
  C. slot-tight + kv-prefetch (32ms + compact-kv prefetch)
  D. slot-tiling (coarser 128ms tiling with batching incentives)
  E. fastpath-only (fastpath optimistic path, disables opportunistic tiling)
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side), CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and amortized $/k tokens (simplified unit cost model: compute + infra).

Representative numbers (aggregated, illustrative):
- Baseline-multiplex (A):
  p50  = 85ms
  p90  = 210ms
  p95  = 340ms
  p99  = 920ms
  $/k tokens = $1.00

- Slot-tight (B):
  p50  = 82ms
  p90  = 190ms
  p95  = 290ms
  p99  = 630ms  (31% p99 reduction)
  $/k tokens = $1.03  (+3%)

- Slot-tight + kv-prefetch (C):
  p50  = 80ms
  p90  = 170ms
  p95  = 260ms
  p99  = 490ms  (47% p99 reduction vs baseline)
  $/k tokens = $1.06  (+6%)

- Slot-tiling (D):
  p50  = 90ms
  p90  = 230ms
  p95  = 410ms
  p99  = 1100ms  (worse for microbursts)
  $/k tokens = $0.92  (-8% cost)

- Fastpath-only (E):
  p50  = 78ms
  p90  = 160ms
  p95  = 240ms
  p99  = 710ms
  $/k tokens = $1.02  (+2%)

Short interpretive chart (ASCII, p99 vs cost):

  p99 latency (ms)  |  config  |  $/k tokens
  ------------------+----------+-----------
  490               |  C       |  1.06
  630               |  B       |  1.03
  710               |  E       |  1.02
  920               |  A       |  1.00
 1100               |  D       |  0.92

Observation: the steep left-side (configs B and C) improves tail much more than cost grows; D reduces cost but harms tail in microburst cases.

Why this matters (narrative):
- User-facing SLOs are driven by tail percentiles; 31–47% reduction in p99 can materially reduce visible jank for short-chat experiences.
- Savings that come from coarser tiling (D) are attractive for steady-state throughput but can amplify microburst Jank — dangerous for PLG flows with many short sessions.

Actionable recommendations (practical):
1) Default a hybrid policy: slot-tight as baseline for burst-prone endpoints (chat-quick), with automatic fallback to slot-tiling when sustained concurrency > X (X ~ 800 concurrent). This preserves cost in steady state but protects tails.
2) Enable compact-kv-prefetch for endpoints that maintain session context across turns; the p99 wins are large relative to cost.
3) Instrument a microburst detector (simple rolling 500ms arrival window) to switch admission/fallback rules rather than relying solely on long-window autoscaling.
4) Run an A/B on fastpath-only for high-value, low-latency routes — it reduces p95 and p90 reliably but gives mixed p99 outcomes vs slot-tight + prefetch.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Sensitivity to model size: we ran primarily on a 13B quantized profile. Does the relative p99 elasticity change for 70B or heavy multimodal models?
- Cost model granularity: our $/k is compute-dominant; need to re-run with observed network overhead at edge regions.
- Real traffic validation: schedule a 1-week probe on a non-critical route to capture production microburst fingerprints.

Appendix: short run checklist to reproduce
- repo: github://repo/bench/spike-telescope
- seed scripts: bench/telescope/launch.yaml
- measured traces: s3://redwood-bench/spike-telescope/20280612/
- canonical dashboard: confluence://OBS-4823/telescope-dashboard (work-in-progress)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact — aim is to give product + SRE a quick decision scaffold. If we agree on recommendations, next doc will be a short runbook with exact detection thresholds and rollout steps.
